tasks.registered_metrics_text:
a) Define the metric(s) to assess a property of an algorithm. These metrics should reflect the desired algorithm
properties described in assessment aim(s) (see above). State which metric(s) were used to compute the ranking(s) (if
any).
  • Example 1: Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC)
  • Example 2: Area under curve (AUC)
We use Average Precision (AP) implemented in sckit (https://scikit-
learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.metrics.average_precision_score.html).

b) Justify why the metric(s) was/were chosen, preferably with reference to the biomedical application.

AP is suggested to be more robust to AUC with regard to class imbalance. Although we expect the class
distribution to be balanced (around 1:1), we used AP considering that the non-diagnostic images occur much less
frequently in clinical practice. We will also compare other metrics (e.g., accuracy and AUC) and present them on
the leaderboard (not for the final ranking).
tasks.registered_ranking_text:
a) Describe the method used to compute a performance rank for all submitted algorithms based on the generated
metric results on the test cases. Typically the text will describe how results obtained per case and metric are aggregated
to arrive at a final score/ranking.

For each case in the validation and test set, participating teams should submit a score in the interval [0-1], where 0
is the lowest score indicating the non-diagnostic quality and 1 is the highest score indicating the diagnostic quality.
Scores above and below the interval [0-1] will be clamped. We calculate the AP between the submission and the


 Extreme Cardiac MRI Analysis Challenge under Respiratory Motion

ground-truth labels provided by the radiologist.

b) Describe the method(s) used to manage submissions with missing results on test cases.

Participating teams are required to submit docker containers and process all the cases in the test set. For the cases
without valid output, we will assign it to 1, i.e., the diagnostic quality in default.

c) Justify why the described ranking scheme(s) was/were used.

AP is a commonly used metric and validated in previous challenges.

tasks.registered_metrics_text:
a) Define the metric(s) to assess a property of an algorithm. These metrics should reflect the desired algorithm
properties described in assessment aim(s) (see above). State which metric(s) were used to compute the ranking(s) (if
any).
  • Example 1: Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC)
  • Example 2: Area under curve (AUC)
We use both Dice score and 95% Hausdorff distance.

b) Justify why the metric(s) was/were chosen, preferably with reference to the biomedical application.

The Dice score gives a measure of volume overlap, while the Hausdorff distance gives a performance measure in
distance.
tasks.registered_ranking_text:
a) Describe the method used to compute a performance rank for all submitted algorithms based on the generated
metric results on the test cases. Typically the text will describe how results obtained per case and metric are aggregated
to arrive at a final score/ranking.

Both the Dice scores and Hausorff distances are used to compute the rankings. For each case, we will compute the
3 Dice scores and 3 95% Hausdorff distance measures between the ground truth and the submitted segmentations
of LV, MYO and RV, respectively. We follow the ranking algorithms in BraTS challenges. For X number of cases
included in the test set, each participant have X*6 rankings. The final ranking score is the average of all these
rankings normalised by the number of teams. It is noted that images with non-diagnostic quality are excluded
from the evaluation of segmentation performance.

b) Describe the method(s) used to manage submissions with missing results on test cases.



 Extreme Cardiac MRI Analysis Challenge under Respiratory Motion

Participating teams are required to submit docker containers and process all the cases in the test set. For the cases
without valid output, we set the ranks for the corresponding metrics to the maximum.

c) Justify why the described ranking scheme(s) was/were used.

The ranking scheme alleviates the influence of a single case and provides more robust ranking results.
